description: The Nature Conservancy — Wetlands Restoration for Ecosystem and Community Resilience in He’eia O’ahu is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF); Kako‘o ‘Ōiwi; He‘eia National Estuarine Research Reserve. To restore function in a degraded but historically, culturally, and ecologically important watershed on O‘ahu’s Eastern Coast, The Nature Conservancy worked closely with local partners and used an adaptive management approach to ensure successful wetland restoration. Coverage: the United States (2022). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
